dialect.label: Heidenhain TNC 640 (Klartext)
dialect.about: Heidenhain's conversational language, Klartext. A block number, then a function and its words: L X+10 Y-5 RL F200 M3 (a line), C and CC (an arc around a center), CR (an arc with a radius), FMAX (rapid). TOOL CALL 5 Z S4000 changes the tool. CYCL DEF sets up a cycle with Q parameters, one to a line ending in ~, and CYCL CALL or M99 runs it. LBL and CALL LBL make subprograms and repeats, and Q parameters hold values.

source.manual: Heidenhain TNC 640 User's Manual Klartext Programming (NC software 34059x-18) and Programming of Machining Cycles
source.section: Program structure, path functions, tools, M functions, labels, cycles, PATTERN DEF and Q parameters; see docs/manual-reviews/heidenhain-tnc640.md

IX: Move this far in X from where the tool is
IY: Move this far in Y from where the tool is
IZ: Move this far in Z from where the tool is
PR: Polar radius from the pole CC
PA: Polar angle around the pole CC
RL: Tool radius compensation, tool on the left
RR: Tool radius compensation, tool on the right
CLSD: Start (+) or end (-) of a closed contour
LA: Number of blocks to look ahead

Q201: Depth from the surface (incremental; the sign gives the direction)
Q204: 2nd set-up clearance, used when it's larger
Q210: Dwell at the top, in seconds
Q211: Dwell at the bottom, in seconds
Q212: How much smaller each plunge gets
Q215: 0 rough and finish, 1 rough only, 2 finish only
Q239: Thread pitch (+ right hand, - left hand)
Q343: 1: depth from the diameter, 0: depth as given
Q367: Where the pocket is from the tool: 0 center, 1 to 4 a corner
Q395: Depth measured to the tip (0) or the cylinder (1)
Q439: What the feed is measured at

BEGIN PGM.desc: Start of the program: its name, then MM or INCH

BLK FORM 0.1.desc: Workpiece blank: the tool axis and the corner with the smallest coordinates

BLK FORM 0.2.desc: Workpiece blank: the corner with the largest coordinates

BLK FORM ROTATION.desc: Workpiece blank turned from a contour

BLK FORM FILE.desc: Workpiece blank from a 3D model file

TOOL CALL.desc: Tool call: the tool, its axis, then the spindle speed, feed and oversizes

TOOL DEF.desc: Tool definition, or the next tool to get ready

LP.desc: Straight line in polar coordinates, from the pole CC

C.desc: Arc around the circle center CC

CC.desc: Circle center and pole (the tool doesn't move)

CT.desc: Arc tangent to the element before

CP.desc: Arc in polar coordinates around the pole CC

RND.desc: Rounds the corner with radius R

CHF.desc: Chamfers the corner, with this side length

APPR LN.desc: Approach along a line at right angles to the first element

APPR LCT.desc: Approach along a line, then a tangent arc

APPR PLT.desc: Approach along a tangent line, in polar coordinates

APPR PLN.desc: Approach along a perpendicular line, in polar coordinates

APPR PCT.desc: Approach along a tangent arc, in polar coordinates

APPR PLCT.desc: Approach along a line then a tangent arc, in polar coordinates

DEP LN.desc: Depart along a line at right angles

DEP LCT.desc: Depart along a tangent arc, then a line

DEP PLCT.desc: Depart along a tangent arc then a line, in polar coordinates

FLT.desc: Free contour line, tangent to the element before

FCT.desc: Free contour arc, tangent to the element before

CYCL DEF.desc: Cycle definition: sets the cycle up without running it

CYCL CALL.desc: Run the defined cycle once, where the tool is

CYCL CALL PAT.desc: Run the defined cycle at every point of the pattern

CYCL CALL POS.desc: Run the defined cycle once at this position

PATTERN DEF.desc: Pattern definition: the points CYCL CALL PAT runs at

LBL.desc: Label: a place a call or a jump goes to

LBL 0.desc: End of a subprogram: go back to the block after the call

CALL LBL.desc: Run the subprogram at this label; with REP, repeat the section from the label this many more times

CALL PGM.desc: Run another program, then come back

CALL SELECTED.desc: Run the program chosen with SEL PGM

SEL.desc: Choose a program, cycle, table or pattern for a later call

FN 1.desc: Sets a Q parameter to a sum

FN 2.desc: Sets a Q parameter to a difference

FN 3.desc: Sets a Q parameter to a product

FN 4.desc: Sets a Q parameter to a quotient

FN 5.desc: Sets a Q parameter to a square root

FN 6.desc: Sets a Q parameter to a sine

FN 7.desc: Sets a Q parameter to a cosine

FN 8.desc: Sets a Q parameter to the root of the sum of two squares

FN 9.desc: Jump to the label if the two values are equal

FN 10.desc: Jump to the label if the two values aren't equal

FN 11.desc: Jump to the label if the first value is greater

FN 12.desc: Jump to the label if the first value is less

FN 13.desc: Sets a Q parameter to an angle

FN 18.desc: Read system data into a Q parameter

M89.desc: Run the cycle after every positioning block, until M99 or a new CYCL DEF

M91.desc: Coordinates in this block are from the machine datum

M92.desc: Coordinates in this block are from the machine preset position

M94.desc: Reduce the rotary axis display to under 360°

M99.desc: Run the cycle once, at the end of this move

M101.desc: Change to a replacement tool when the tool life runs out

M103.desc: Plunge feed as a percentage (F); alone, cancels

M107.desc: Don't stop for a positive tool oversize

M108.desc: Stop again for a positive tool oversize

M109.desc: Constant feed at the cutting edge on arcs

M110.desc: Constant feed at the cutting edge on inside arcs only

M116.desc: Feed on rotary axes in mm/min

M120.desc: Look ahead LA blocks for radius compensation

M126.desc: Rotary axes take the shorter way

M128.desc: Keep the tool tip position when tilting axes move

M130.desc: Coordinates in this block are in the untilted system

M137.desc: Feed in mm per minute again

M140.desc: Retract along the tool axis (MB the distance, MB MAX to the limit)

M148.desc: Lift the tool off at an NC stop
